introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: Answer ALL the questions in the spaces provided (10 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: Answer ALL FOUR questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given an acute angle $\Theta$, where $\sin\Theta=\dfrac12$.

a) Find the value of $\Theta$ in degrees.
b) Evaluate $\cos\Theta$ to 2 decimal places. *[4 marks for (i)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With $\Theta=30^\circ$: $\cos30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=0.8660\ldots$

Check with a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $2$ and opposite side $1$: the adjacent side is $\sqrt{2^2-1^2}=\sqrt3$, so $\cos\Theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

To $2$ decimal places: $0.87$.

**Answer: $\cos\Theta\approx0.87$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) A sequence is given as $2, 5, 8, \ldots$

Find:

a) the common difference of the sequence.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Subtract a term from the next one: $5-2=3$ and $8-5=3$.

**Answer: the common difference is $d=3$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: b) the $5^{\text{th}}$ term of the sequence.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The sequence is arithmetic with first term $a=2$ and $d=3$: $T_n=a+(n-1)d$.

$T_5=2+(5-1)\times3=2+12=14$.

Check by listing: $2,\ 5,\ 8,\ 11,\ 14$.

**Answer: the $5^{\text{th}}$ term is $14$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: c) the sum of the first 5 terms. *[6 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$S_n=\dfrac n2(a+l)$ with $n=5$, first term $2$ and last term $14$:

$S_5=\dfrac52(2+14)=\dfrac52\times16=40$.

Check by adding: $2+5+8+11+14=40$.

**Answer: the sum of the first $5$ terms is $40$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) Using a pencil, a ruler and a pair of compasses only,

a) draw a circle of radius 4 cm.
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Mark a point $O$ for the centre.
2. Open the compasses to exactly $4$ cm (check against the ruler).
3. With the point of the compasses on $O$, draw a complete circle.

questions.enonce_markdown: b) mark a point $P$ on the circumference and construct a chord $PQ=6$ cm.
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Mark any point $P$ on the circle.
2. Open the compasses to exactly $6$ cm.
3. With the point of the compasses on $P$, draw an arc that cuts the circle. Call this point $Q$.
4. Join $P$ to $Q$ with the ruler: $PQ=6$ cm is a chord of the circle.

1. Keep the compasses open at $6$ cm.
2. With the point of the compasses on $Q$, draw an arc that cuts the circle. It cuts the circle at $P$ and at a second point: call the second point $R$.
3. Join $Q$ to $R$ with the ruler: $QR=6$ cm is a second chord, with $R\neq P$.

Join $P$ to $R$ with the ruler. Leave all construction arcs visible.

The chords $PQ$ and $QR$ are equal, so $Q$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $PR$. The chord $PR$ is longer than $6$ cm: each $6$ cm chord subtends an angle $2\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac34\right)\approx97.2^\circ$ at $O$, so $PR$ subtends $360^\circ-2\times97.2^\circ=165.6^\circ$ and $PR=2\times4\times\sin(82.8^\circ)\approx7.9$ cm.

When you measure $PR$ on your drawing you should find about $7.9$ cm.
